In the usa, if you fail to show up they put you back in the list of possibles for the next go round. If you skip twice you'll either get a personal summons for failure to show or a letter where you have to explain why you skipped.

You'll fill out paperwork when you get there including a questionnaire about how you would look at or respond to specific incidents. Last time I went, I found 2 grammar mistakes in the questionnaire (county courthouse) and fixed them on the paper before handing in. The lawyers on both sides will see that questionnaire as they try to narrow down the selection.

They eventually will pull you in the courtroom with a judge who will explain the outline of the case and parties involved. They'll ask if you heard about the case in any form and what is was or if you personally know anyone involved.

They will proceed to other parties that have affiliations. They'll list the lawyers / firms and if you are a client etc.

My advice is to answer the questions as precise as possible. Ie, "I read about this incident in the paper." "Mr. Jones is my laywer." Not "Mr Jones is my family lawyer who is helping me with xyz."

Eventually they will decide on the 12 and 2 jurors.
